title: platform-systems-services-comprehensive-playbook-2025-q2
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Purpose and scope:

This document is the canonical Platform Systems & Services playbook for the eng-platform team. It combines: system ownership, how-tos for common tasks, dashboards & alerts definitions, runbooks for high-impact incidents, retrospective guidance, and a 12-month roadmap for platform priorities. Intended audience: platform engineers, on-call SREs, product engineering partners, and platform support.

1) High-level system map (owner + responsibilities)
- control-plane-api (owner: platform-api team): routing, auth, feature flags, schema validation, SLO: 99.9% p95 latency < 120ms
- telemetry-ingest (owner: observability-team): metrics/traces ingest and enrichment, SLO: 99.95% retention for 7d
- platform-orchestrator (owner: runtime-orchestration): autoscaling, actor placement, SLO: 99.9% reconciliation within 60s
- service-catalog (owner: platform-services): discovery, config, model metadata store, TTL backups daily

2) Dashboards and key metrics (owners and query hints)
- Control Plane Overview (owner: platform-api): requests/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, auth failures (per-region)
- Capacity & Scheduling (owner: runtime-op): GPU utilization, queued requests, average batch size, eviction rate
- Telemetry Health (owner: observability): span ingestion lag, indexing errors, storage growth rate
- Cost & Efficiency (owner: platform-finops): tokens served per hour, billing anomalies, per-model unit cost

Suggested dashboard panels and alert knobs:
| Panel | Recommended threshold | Severity | Owner |
| Control plane p95 latency | > 200ms for 5m | P2 | platform-api |
| 5xx rate | > 0.5% sustained 10m | P1 | platform-api |
| GPU utilization (cluster) | > 90% sustained 15m | P2 | runtime-op |
| Queue depth | > 1000 requests for 5m | P1 | runtime-op |
| Telemetry ingestion lag | > 2m backlog | P2 | observability |

3) Alerting policy and escalation (step-by-step)
1. Pager triggers when alert is P1 (critical): notify oncall via PagerDuty, channel #oncall-incident, and send SMS to primary.
2. Oncall triage (first 10 minutes): acknowledge, set incident bridge, capture: symptoms, start time, suspected service, triage owner.
3. Mitigation (10-30 minutes): apply runbook steps below; if mitigation unsuccessful escalate to L2 and rotation to L3 after 30 minutes.
4. Postmortem: create incident page in /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems within 72 hours, assign author and reviewers.

4) Runbooks (playbook entries for common high-impact scenarios)
A. Control plane slow / high 5xxs- Preconditions: Dashboard shows p95>200ms and 5xx rate >0.5%- Steps:
  1) Confirm root cause: check service logs (elk), recent deploys (CI pipeline dashboard), and feature flag changes
  2) If deploy caused regression: rollback last successful release (CI job: rollback-control-plane) and scale up canary instances
  3) If resource exhaustion: scale control-plane replicas by +30% and open autoscaling group
  4) Notify product owners and operations
  5) Record mitigation actions and timeline in incident bridge notes

B. GPU backlog and scheduling failures- Preconditions: queue depth > 1000 or batch size drop < 2 tokens- Steps:
  1) Verify orchestrator health (k8s pods, reconciliation logs) and node conditions (OOM, disk pressure)
  2) Temporarily drain low-priority pools and reassign critical capacity using runtime-orchestrator CLI: runtimectl reassign --pool critical --from low-priority --count 4
  3) Enable burst capacity policy (owner: runtime-op) to accept short-term load for 30m
  4) If scheduling still fails, provision emergency nodes via cloud-ops runbook (cloud account credentials in Vault)

5) How-tos (operational recipes)
- Onboard a new platform service:
  1) Create service entry in service-catalog (schema: name, owner, SLA, runbook_link)
  2) Add dashboards and alerts using templates in /dashboards/templates
  3) Run e2e smoke tests (CI job: smoke-service) and sign off with product engineer
- Add a dashboard panel:
  1) Copy template JSON from /dashboards/templates/panel-template.json
  2) Update metric query and thresholds, set owner, add to Control Plane Overview
  3) Request review from observability-team via PR in grafana-configs repo

6) Retrospective guidance (post-incident)
- Timeline expectations: draft within 72 hours, final within 10 business days
- Required sections: summary, impact, timeline, root cause(s), mitigation, follow-ups (owner + due date), lessons learned
- Example follow-ups: increase retention for telemetry by 2 days (owner: observability, due: 2026-03-01), improve canary rollout automation (owner: platform-api, due: 2026-04-15)

7) 12-month platform roadmap (top-level milestones)
- Q3 2025: GA rollout of autoscaling policies and burst capacity controls; reduce cold-start p99 by 30%
- Q4 2025: Launch platform cost & model-efficiency dashboard; pilot quantization profile recommendations in Redwood Optimize
- Q1 2026: Private deployment CI/CD hardened for air-gapped installs; integrate KMS/HSM for edge customers
- Q2 2026: SLA improvements for Dedicated customers (target 99.95% uptime), improved multi-region failover

8) Ownership, SLAs and run frequency
- Weekly: platform platform-ops sync (review alerts > P2, open follow-ups)
- Monthly: reliability review (SLO burn rate, error budgets) owned by eng-sre
- Quarterly: roadmap and postmortem review with product and customer-success teams

9) Reference artifacts and links
- Dashboards templates: /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards/templates
- Grafana config repo: git@github.com:redwood-inference/grafana-configs.git
- Runbook automation tools: /tools/runtimectl and /tools/incident-bot
- Incident postmortem template: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortem-template

10) Appendix: configuration snippets and common CLI commands
- runtimectl status --service control-plane-api --output json- runtimectl reassign --pool critical --from low-priority --count 4- terraform apply -target=module.gpu_cluster -var-file=env/prod.tfvars
